checklist.step: Pull the quarterly conduct-metrics data set
actions: Ask Regulatory Reporting to extract enrollee complaint counts, complaint types and resolution days from the complaint tracking system for the quarter.
In the BI/reporting platform open the Market Conduct dashboard and refresh the complaint ratio, prompt-pay timeliness and network adequacy tiles for the individual-market book.
Pull incurred claims and premium by rating area from the claims warehouse to seed the running Medical Loss Ratio calculation.
Confirm the enrollment count used in the complaint ratio denominator ties to the CMS enrollment reconciliation file for the same period.
checklist.done: the quarterly data set (complaints, network adequacy, running MLR) is pulled and ties to the CMS enrollment reconciliation.

checklist.step: Compare each metric to its regulatory benchmark
actions: Compare the NAIC complaint index (complaints per 1,000 covered lives) to the state DOI benchmark and to the prior four quarters.
Compare the running MLR to the 80% individual-market floor in 45 CFR 158.
Check the EHB annual/lifetime dollar-limit scan for any claim adjudicated against a plan-level or lifetime cap, which 45 CFR 147.126/156.410 prohibit outright.
Check network adequacy time/distance results against the state's access standard and the CMS QHP network adequacy template.
checklist.done: every metric has a benchmark comparison recorded with a pass/fail flag.

checklist.step: Investigate any metric outside benchmark
actions: For a complaint-ratio breach, pull the underlying complaint files and categorize by root cause (claims denial, enrollment error, network access).
For an MLR shortfall, ask the Pricing Actuary whether it reflects a genuine loss-ratio trend or a data feed error.
For any EHB dollar-limit hit, pull the claim and adjudication log and confirm whether the system, not the plan design, applied the cap in error.
Document the finding on the quarterly metrics workpaper with supporting extracts attached.
checklist.done: every out-of-benchmark metric has a documented root-cause finding.

checklist.step: Escalate confirmed EHB dollar-limit violations immediately
actions: Any confirmed lifetime/annual dollar limit applied to an essential health benefit is escalated same-day to the Compliance Officer and Regulatory Counsel — a strict-liability breach under 45 CFR 156.410/156.420, not a benchmark miss.
Open a remediation case in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with the member, claim number and dollar amount improperly capped.
Direct the Claims Platform to reprocess the claim without the limit and confirm the corrected payment.
Notify the affected member per the plan's error-correction procedure.
checklist.done: every confirmed EHB-limit violation has a same-day escalation, a reprocessed claim and a member notice.

checklist.step: Calculate the preliminary MLR by rating category
actions: In the MLR calculation worksheet, compute incurred claims plus quality-improvement expense divided by earned premium (net of taxes/fees), separately for individual and any small-group business.
Apply the credibility adjustment for the issuer's member-life count per the MLR credibility table in 45 CFR 158.230.
Cross-check earned premium to the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) annual statement Exhibit of Premiums, Enrollment and Utilization.
Flag any rating category tracking below the 80% floor for rebate calculation.
checklist.done: a credibility-adjusted MLR is computed per rating category and reconciled to the NAIC annual statement.

checklist.step: Compute the rebate owed for any category below the floor
actions: For each rating category below 80% MLR, compute rebate = (80% − actual MLR) × earned premium, per the 45 CFR 158.240 formula.
Allocate the category rebate to individual enrollees pro-rata to premium paid during the MLR reporting year.
Have the Appointed Actuary review the rebate computation and credibility adjustment for reasonableness.
Save the rebate workpaper with the per-enrollee allocation schedule.
checklist.done: a per-enrollee rebate schedule exists, reviewed by the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: File the MLR Annual Reporting Form with CMS
actions: Complete the MLR Annual Reporting Form in the CMS MLR data-collection module (accessed through the CMS CCIIO Health Insurance Oversight System) with premium, claims, expense and rebate figures by state and market.
Attach the credibility adjustment and rebate calculation detail as supporting schedules.
Submit before the CMS MLR filing deadline (July 31 following the reporting year) and log the system-generated confirmation number in the Internal Regulatory System.
Reconcile the submitted totals back to the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) annual statement figures line by line.
checklist.done: the MLR Annual Reporting Form is submitted to CMS with a retained confirmation number reconciled to the NAIC statement.

checklist.step: Issue rebates to enrollees by September 30
actions: Generate the rebate payment file (check or premium credit) from the per-enrollee allocation schedule.
Where the rebate is under the de minimis threshold in 45 CFR 158.243, apply it as a premium credit instead of a check per the regulation's election rules.
Issue payments/credits through the Payment Gateway and confirm posting to each enrollee's account.
Send the CMS-prescribed rebate notice to every enrollee receiving a rebate, using the model notice language.
checklist.done: every rebate is paid or credited by September 30 with a CMS-compliant notice sent.

checklist.step: Log any missed benchmark or late rebate as an exception
actions: Open a tracker record for any benchmark miss, EHB violation or rebate issued after September 30.
Record root cause, dollar/member impact and the remediation owner.
Set a remediation due date and link the underlying workpaper.
Route EHB-limit and late-rebate exceptions to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report assessment.
checklist.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, due date and a counsel assessment where required.

checklist.step: Refresh the quarterly conduct-metrics report for leadership
actions: Compile the quarter's benchmark results, exceptions and remediation status into the Market Conduct Committee report.
Include the current MLR trend and projected rebate exposure ahead of the September 30 deadline.
Present at the quarterly Market Conduct Committee meeting and record attendance and discussion notes.
File the report and minutes in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is presented to the Market Conduct Committee and filed with minutes.

checklist.step: Update the compliance procedure on any CMS bulletin change
actions: Monitor CMS CCIIO bulletins and the Federal Register for changes to MLR formulas, credibility tables or EHB dollar-limit guidance.
Redline the Conduct Metrics Monitoring Procedure to reflect the change.
Route the redline to the Compliance Officer's leadership for re-approval.
Communicate the change to Regulatory Reporting Analyst and Billing Operations Manager before the next reporting cycle.
checklist.done: the procedure reflects the current CMS guidance and is re-approved before the next cycle.

checklist.step: Reconcile complaint-file evidence to the reported complaint ratio
actions: Sample 10 complaints from the quarter and confirm each is present in both the complaint tracking system and the BI dashboard count.
Confirm resolution days recorded match the closed-date fields in the complaint file.
Note any complaint miscategorized as non-reportable and correct the ratio.
Attach the reconciliation to the quarterly workpaper.
checklist.done: the sampled complaints reconcile between source system and reported ratio, or a correction is logged.

checklist.step: Retain the metric reports and MLR workpapers
actions: File the quarterly metric reports, MLR calculation workpapers, CMS submission confirmation and rebate schedules in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label required by 45 CFR 158.502.
Index by reporting year and market so records are retrievable for a CMS audit.
checklist.done: all quarter and annual MLR records are filed, retention-labeled and indexed by year and market.

checklist.step: Brief the Appointed Actuary on any structural loss-ratio trend
actions: Where the MLR trend suggests a pricing or product-design issue rather than a one-off, brief the Appointed Actuary and Pricing Actuary.
Request an assessment of whether the next rate filing needs to reflect the trend.
Record the assessment outcome in the quarterly workpaper.
checklist.done: a documented actuarial assessment exists for any structural MLR trend.

checklist.step: Certify the annual conduct-metrics cycle complete
actions: Confirm every quarter's benchmark review, the MLR filing, rebate issuance and all exceptions are closed or have an open remediation date.
Sign the annual certification memo confirming the cycle met the September 30 rebate deadline.
File the certification with the compliance evidence repository and report to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: a signed annual certification exists confirming the cycle closed on or before September 30 with all exceptions tracked.

testing.step: Build the population of quarterly metrics and MLR filings
actions: Extract all quarterly benchmark records and the annual MLR filing/rebate records for the audit period from the BI/reporting platform and the compliance evidence repository.
Include every rating category and state within the individual market.
Reconcile the extract count to the number of Market Conduct Committee reports issued in the period.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to committee reporting records.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the complaint tracking and claims source systems
actions: Match a sample of reported complaint counts back to the complaint tracking system record by record.
Match reported incurred claims to the claims warehouse extract used in the MLR calculation.
List any unreconciled figures as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: sampled complaint and claims figures reconcile to source systems or are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of quarters with a benchmark breach or EHB-limit finding.
Take a random sample of 2 additional quarters (seeded, reproducible) from the remaining population.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every breach quarter.

testing.step: Re-perform the MLR calculation for the sampled quarters
actions: Independently recompute the credibility-adjusted MLR from the underlying claims/premium extract for each sampled rating category.
Compare to the recorded MLR; any variance beyond rounding is an exception.
Recompute the rebate owed and compare to the paid amount.
testing.done: independently recomputed MLR and rebate match the recorded figures or are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Trace the MLR filing to the CMS confirmation
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System pull the logged CMS confirmation number for the sampled year's MLR Annual Reporting Form.
Confirm the confirmation date pre-dates the July 31 CMS filing deadline.
Confirm the submitted totals match the recomputed MLR and rebate figures.
testing.done: each sampled MLR filing traces to a CMS confirmation submitted on time with matching figures.

testing.step: Verify rebate payment timing and notices
actions: For a sample of enrollee rebate records, confirm the Payment Gateway posting date is on or before September 30.
Confirm the CMS-prescribed rebate notice was sent to each sampled enrollee.
Confirm de minimis rebates were applied as premium credits per 45 CFR 158.243, not omitted.
testing.done: sampled rebates were paid or credited by September 30 with notices sent.

testing.step: Test EHB annual/lifetime dollar-limit compliance
actions: Pull a sample of high-dollar claims across the audit period and confirm none were adjudicated against a lifetime or annual dollar cap.
Where a prior violation was found, confirm the claim was reprocessed and the member notified.
Confirm the reprocessed payment amount matches the corrected adjudication.
testing.done: no sampled high-dollar claim shows an EHB dollar-limit violation, or the violation was corrected and evidenced.

testing.step: Confirm complaint-ratio benchmarking method
actions: Recompute the complaint ratio for a sampled quarter using the enrollment reconciliation file as the denominator.
Compare to the reported ratio and the state DOI benchmark used.
Flag any denominator or benchmark-source discrepancy.
testing.done: recomputed complaint ratio matches the reported figure and benchmark source.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception found in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner distinct from the original preparer.
Set a remediation date and, for EHB or late-rebate breaches, confirm a self-report assessment was completed.
Carry open exceptions into the next testing cycle as mandatory retest items.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold for EHB-limit violations and the on-time threshold for rebates.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who did not perform the original quarterly monitoring, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Market Conduct Committee and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the standing exam-readiness file library and assigns section owners

checklist.step: Define the exam-readiness file taxonomy
actions: Map the taxonomy to the categories a CMS or state DOI market-conduct exam typically requests: complaint handling, claims processing, underwriting/rating (single risk pool), network adequacy, marketing/sales, risk-adjustment data validation.
In the GRC platform, create a binder folder per category with a named owner and refresh cadence.
Cross-reference each folder to the citation it supports, for example the underwriting/rating folder cites 45 CFR 156.80.
Circulate the taxonomy to all section owners for acknowledgement.
checklist.done: a GRC binder exists with a named owner, cadence and citation for every exam category.

checklist.step: Assemble the single risk pool rate-development workpapers
actions: Pull the market-wide index rate build-up for the individual market, showing every non-grandfathered plan's experience pooled per 45 CFR 156.80.
Attach the rate filing's Unified Rate Review Template and actuarial memorandum that documents the single-risk-pool methodology.
Confirm no plan's experience was rated outside the pool without a permitted adjustment such as the catastrophic-plan pooling rule.
File the workpaper set in the GRC binder's underwriting/rating folder.
checklist.done: the single risk pool workpaper set is complete and filed with the supporting rate filing.

checklist.step: Assemble HHS-RADV risk-adjustment data validation results
actions: Pull the issuer's most recent HHS-RADV initial and second-validation-sample results and the resulting risk-score adjustment.
Attach the medical record review vendor's discrepancy report and the issuer's error-rate calculation.
Confirm the risk-adjustment transfer amount posted to the general ledger matches the CMS-published transfer report.
File in the risk-adjustment folder with the CMS transfer summary report.
checklist.done: HHS-RADV results and the reconciled transfer amount are filed together.

checklist.step: Assemble the complaint-handling file set
actions: Pull every consumer complaint received in the period from the complaint tracking system, including DOI-referred and CMS-referred complaints.
Attach the intake log, investigation notes, and resolution letter for each.
Confirm resolution timeliness against the state's prompt-complaint-response standard.
File chronologically in the complaint-handling folder.
checklist.done: the complaint folder holds every complaint with intake, investigation and resolution evidence.

checklist.step: Assemble network adequacy and QHP certification records
actions: Pull the current plan year's network adequacy time/distance results as submitted with the QHP application.
Attach the CMS QHP certification confirmation and any state network adequacy waiver.
Confirm the provider directory accuracy audit results are attached and current within the last quarter.
File in the network adequacy folder.
checklist.done: network adequacy and certification records are current and filed with the provider directory audit.

checklist.step: Refresh each folder on its assigned cadence
actions: Follow the GRC platform task list for folders due for monthly refresh.
Pull the latest extract from the relevant source system (claims, enrollment, rating) for each due folder.
Replace superseded documents, retaining prior versions in a dated subfolder rather than deleting them.
Mark the GRC task complete with the refresh date.
checklist.done: every folder due in the period is refreshed with dated version history retained.

checklist.step: Confirm every filed document is source-traceable
actions: Spot-check 5 documents per folder for a visible source system, extract date and preparer name.
Reject and re-source any document lacking traceability.
Log the check date on the folder's cover sheet.
checklist.done: every sampled document in each folder is traceable to its source and extract date.

checklist.step: Identify and close readiness gaps
actions: Compare the taxonomy checklist to the binder contents and list any missing or stale (older than one refresh cycle) section.
Open a tracker record for each gap with an owner and closure date.
Escalate any gap open longer than two refresh cycles to the Compliance Officer.
Close the tracker record once the section owner confirms the refreshed document is filed.
checklist.done: every readiness gap is tracked to closure with an owner and date.

checklist.step: Run a mock exam-request drill annually
actions: Simulate a CMS or state DOI document request covering three exam categories chosen at random.
Time how long it takes each section owner to produce the requested documents from the binder.
Record any category that misses the 5-business-day response standard as a readiness finding.
Report drill results to the Market Conduct Committee.
checklist.done: an annual mock drill is completed with response times recorded and reported.

checklist.step: Maintain the exam-response contact and escalation list
actions: Confirm the current section owner, backup, and Regulatory Counsel contact for each binder folder.
Update the list whenever a section owner changes role.
Store the list at the front of the GRC binder.
Verify contact accuracy at each quarterly refresh.
checklist.done: the contact list is current as of the last quarterly refresh.

checklist.step: Coordinate with Regulatory Counsel on privileged material
actions: Review the binder for any document that should be marked attorney work product, such as self-critical exam-prep memos.
Tag privileged documents distinctly in the GRC platform so they are withheld or produced only on counsel's direction during an actual exam.
Confirm no privileged document is filed in a folder that would auto-produce.
checklist.done: privileged documents are tagged and segregated from the standard production set.

checklist.step: Open the binder for an actual exam and log the request-response cycle
actions: On receipt of an exam notice, open an exam case in the GRC platform referencing the binder.
Log every document request received and the date/section owner who produced the response.
Track response time against the regulator's stated deadline for that request.
Route any request touching privileged material to Regulatory Counsel before production.
checklist.done: every exam document request is logged with a response date and, where applicable, counsel review.

checklist.step: Retain exam correspondence and findings
actions: File the exam notice, all document requests/responses, and the final exam report/findings letter in the GRC binder's exam-history folder.
Apply the 7-year (or through-resolution) retention label.
Cross-reference any finding to the remediation item opened under the exam-findings remediation process.
checklist.done: exam correspondence and findings are filed with retention labels and cross-referenced to remediation.

checklist.step: Certify continuous readiness at each quarter-end
actions: Review the tracker for open readiness gaps and confirm none is older than the escalation threshold.
Sign a quarterly readiness certification memo.
File the certification in the GRC binder's governance folder.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly readiness certification exists with no unescalated aged gaps.

checklist.step: Retire and archive prior plan-year binders
actions: At each plan-year rollover, move the prior year's binder into an archive folder in the GRC platform.
Confirm the archive retains full document history and retention labels.
Start a fresh current-year binder from the taxonomy template.
checklist.done: the prior plan-year binder is archived intact and a fresh current-year binder is started.

testing.step: Build the population of exam-readiness folders and refresh events
actions: Extract every binder folder and its logged refresh events for the test period from the GRC platform.
Include any exam cases opened in the period.
Reconcile the folder count to the approved taxonomy list.
testing.done: population reconciled to the approved taxonomy and logged refresh events.

testing.step: Reconcile refresh cadence compliance
actions: For each folder, compare the actual refresh dates to the assigned cadence.
List any folder that missed its cadence by more than one cycle as an exception.
Note whether a missed cadence coincided with a section-owner change, which is a common root cause.
testing.done: cadence compliance is confirmed or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of folders touched by an actual exam in the period.
Take a random sample of 8 additional folders (seeded, reproducible) from the remaining population.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible, covering all exam-touched folders.

testing.step: Re-verify source traceability on the sample
actions: Open each sampled document and confirm the source system, extract date and preparer are legible and correct.
Trace a sub-sample of single risk pool and HHS-RADV documents back to the source rate filing and CMS transfer report.
Log any document that fails traceability.
testing.done: sampled documents trace to source or are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform the single risk pool pooling test
actions: Pull the plan-level experience data underlying the sampled rate filing.
Confirm every non-grandfathered individual-market plan's experience was pooled into the market-wide index rate with no unsupported carve-out.
Flag any plan rated outside the pool without a documented permitted adjustment.
testing.done: pooling is confirmed correct on the sample, or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Confirm the HHS-RADV transfer reconciliation
actions: Compare the filed risk-adjustment transfer amount to the CMS-published transfer report for the sampled plan year.
Trace the general ledger posting to the same amount.
Log any variance as an exception.
testing.done: transfer amounts reconcile across CMS report, filed workpaper and general ledger, or a variance is logged.

testing.step: Test the mock exam-drill response times
actions: Review the most recent mock drill record and confirm response times were logged for all three tested categories.
Re-time one category live by requesting the section owner produce the binder documents.
Compare against the 5-business-day standard.
testing.done: mock drill and live re-test response times are within standard or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Test privileged-document segregation
actions: Sample 5 documents tagged privileged and confirm they are correctly withheld from the standard-production view in the GRC platform.
Sample 5 non-privileged documents and confirm none was mistakenly tagged privileged, which would block a timely regulator response.
Log any mis-tagged document as a finding and have Regulatory Counsel correct the tag immediately.
testing.done: privileged tagging is accurate on both samples or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception found in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner distinct from the section owner tested.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into the next test cycle.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the readiness threshold of no folder more than one cycle stale.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who maintains no binder folder personally, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Market Conduct Committee and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion exists and is reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Intake the finding and open a CAP record
actions: Log the finding from the exam report/findings letter into the GRC platform as a child record of the exam case, capturing the CFR/citation, the regulator's stated requirement and the regulator-set response deadline.
Assign a unique CAP ID and route it to the Compliance Officer for triage.
Confirm the finding letter itself is attached to the record.
Notify the process owner named in the finding, such as the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager or Product Filing Specialist, that a CAP has been opened against their area.
checklist.done: a CAP record exists with citation, deadline, finding letter attached and an assigned process owner.

checklist.step: Perform root-cause analysis
actions: Interview the process owner and pull the underlying transaction/file that triggered the finding.
Classify the root cause: procedure gap, training gap, system defect, one-off human error, or undetected historical practice.
Assess whether the root cause is isolated or affects other products/states, and if so scope the affected population.
Record the root-cause analysis on the CAP record.
checklist.done: a documented root cause and affected-population scope exists on the CAP record.

checklist.step: Draft the corrective action plan
actions: Define the corrective action — procedure fix, system fix, retraining, or look-back remediation — with a named owner and target date for each action item.
Where the root cause affects a broader population, include a look-back remediation plan such as reprocessing affected claims or reissuing notices.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the plan before submission to the regulator.
checklist.done: a CAP with named owners, target dates and, where needed, a look-back plan is drafted and counsel-reviewed.

checklist.step: Submit the CAP to the regulator and negotiate the due date
actions: Submit the CAP to CMS or the state DOI through the channel specified in the finding letter.
Negotiate the regulator-agreed remediation due date and record it as the CAP record's official due date.
File the regulator's CAP acceptance letter on the CAP record.
checklist.done: the CAP is submitted and the regulator-agreed due date is recorded with the acceptance letter attached.

checklist.step: Execute the procedure/system corrective actions
actions: Implement the procedure change, system fix or control identified in the CAP.
Retrain affected staff and log attendance where retraining is an action item.
Update the relevant compliance procedure document to reflect the fix.
Attach the updated procedure and training log to the CAP record.
checklist.done: every corrective action item is implemented with evidence attached to the CAP record.

checklist.step: Execute look-back remediation where the root cause affected other cases
actions: Pull the full population matching the root-cause pattern using the date range and criteria from the CAP.
Reprocess claims, reissue notices, or otherwise correct every affected case in the Claims Platform.
Track completion on a look-back tracker linked to the CAP record.
Confirm 100% of the affected population is remediated before closing the look-back action item.
checklist.done: the full look-back population is remediated and tracked to 100% completion.

checklist.step: Validate the fix operates correctly before closing
actions: Independently test the fixed procedure or system control against a sample of transactions processed after the fix date.
Confirm no recurrence of the original finding in the sample.
Document the validation test and result on the CAP record.
checklist.done: an independent post-fix validation confirms no recurrence in the tested sample.

checklist.step: Assemble the closure evidence package
actions: Compile the corrective action evidence, look-back completion record and the independent validation test into a closure package.
Confirm every CAP action item shows a completion date on or before its target date.
Route the package to the Compliance Officer for sign-off.
checklist.done: a complete closure package with all action items evidenced is ready for sign-off.

checklist.step: Obtain Compliance Officer sign-off before reporting closure
actions: Review the closure package against the original CAP commitments.
Sign the CAP record as closed only if every action item and the validation test are satisfied.
Return the package for rework if any item is incomplete.
checklist.done: the CAP record carries a dated Compliance Officer sign-off with no open action items.

checklist.step: Report closure to the regulator
actions: Submit the CAP closure letter to CMS or the state DOI referencing the original finding and CAP ID.
Attach the closure evidence package or the summary the regulator requires.
File the regulator's closure acknowledgment on the CAP record.
checklist.done: closure is reported to the regulator with an acknowledgment filed.

checklist.step: Track every CAP item's due date on the remediation calendar
actions: Enter every open CAP's regulator-agreed due date into the GRC platform calendar.
Set escalation reminders at T-30/T-14/T-3 days.
Flag any item at risk of missing its due date to the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: every open CAP is on the remediation calendar with active reminders.

checklist.step: Escalate any at-risk or missed CAP due date
actions: Log an exception the moment a CAP item is flagged at risk.
Assess whether a regulator extension request is warranted and, if so, have Regulatory Counsel request it before the due date passes.
Escalate any item that actually misses its due date to the Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
Record the outcome — extension granted, missed with self-report, or closed on time — on the CAP record.
checklist.done: every at-risk or missed CAP has a logged exception and a recorded outcome.

checklist.step: Run the annual September 30 open-items review
actions: Before September 30 each year, pull every CAP item still open across all exams.
Confirm each has a current due date, an owner and an up-to-date status.
Present the open-items summary to the Compliance Committee ahead of Open Enrollment readiness sign-off.
checklist.done: an annual open-items review is completed and reported to the Compliance Committee by September 30.

checklist.step: Retain CAP records for the full retention period
actions: File the finding letter, CAP submission, corrective evidence, validation test and closure acknowledgment in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-closure retention label.
Index by exam ID and CAP ID for retrievability.
checklist.done: CAP records are filed, retention-labeled and indexed by exam and CAP ID.

checklist.step: Feed closed findings into the exam-readiness binder as a control-improvement record
actions: Cross-reference the closed CAP to the relevant exam-readiness binder folder so the fix is visible in future exam prep.
Note the finding and fix in the folder's control-history log.
Confirm the updated procedure referenced in the CAP is the version currently filed in the binder.
checklist.done: the exam-readiness binder reflects the closed finding and the current, fixed procedure version.

testing.step: Build the population of CAP items opened and due in the test period
actions: Extract every CAP record opened or with a due date inside the test period.
Include items still open at period end.
Reconcile the count to the number of findings listed in exam reports received during the period.
testing.done: population reconciles to exam-report finding counts.

testing.step: Reconcile CAP due dates to the regulator's acceptance letters
actions: Match each CAP record's recorded due date to the date stated in the regulator's CAP acceptance letter.
List any mismatch as an exception.
Confirm any date extension granted after the original acceptance letter is itself documented in a follow-up regulator communication.
testing.done: due dates reconcile to acceptance letters or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of CAP items that missed their due date or required a look-back remediation.
Take a random sample of 5 additional items (seeded, reproducible) from the remaining population.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible, covering all missed-deadline and look-back items.

testing.step: Re-perform root-cause and corrective-action adequacy review
actions: Independently assess whether the documented root cause explains the finding and whether the corrective action actually addresses it.
Flag any corrective action that only addresses the symptom, such as one file corrected, without fixing the underlying cause.
Interview the process owner to confirm the corrective action was actually implemented as described, not just documented.
testing.done: corrective-action adequacy is confirmed on the sample or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Re-test the fixed control
actions: Independently pull transactions processed after the CAP's fix date for the sampled item.
Test for recurrence of the original finding pattern.
Compare to the original post-fix validation on file.
testing.done: no recurrence found in independent re-test, or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Verify look-back remediation completeness
actions: For sampled items with a look-back, recompute the affected population using the CAP's stated criteria.
Confirm the look-back tracker shows 100% of that population remediated.
Trace 5 individual look-back cases to their remediation evidence in the Claims Platform.
testing.done: look-back population and remediation evidence agree, or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Confirm regulator reporting and acknowledgment
actions: Confirm the CAP closure letter was sent to the regulator for each sampled closed item.
Confirm a regulator acknowledgment is on file.
Flag any closed CAP with no regulator acknowledgment on file.
testing.done: closure reporting and acknowledgment are on file for every sampled closed item.

testing.step: Recompute the on-time closure rate
actions: For the full population, compute the percentage of CAP items closed on or before their regulator-agreed due date.
Compare to the internal target of 100% on-time or documented extension.
Confirm every late item has an extension request or a self-report on file.
testing.done: the on-time closure rate is computed and every late item is supported by an extension or self-report.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception found in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner distinct from the original CAP owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into the next quarterly test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the on-time closure threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no sampled CAP, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee ahead of the September 30 open-items review and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion exists and feeds the September 30 committee review.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the filing-determination call for every ACA individual-market form/rate/rule change; escalates ambiguous calls to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 45 CFR 154.215 (rate filing justification content) and 45 CFR 154.200/154.230 (rate review program scope and unreasonable-rate-increase threshold), re-read against the current CMS rate review preamble and any effective-rate-review-state list update

In-scope processes.value: Intake of every proposed individual-market rate, form or benefit-design/rule change through the filing-requirement determination gate, before any change reaches product build

In-scope systems.value: Determination logged in the filing tracker; SERFF Filing Rules used to confirm each state's ACA-specific TOI requirements

Compliance procedure documented.value: ACA Filing Determination Procedure — intake, URRT applicability screen, effective-rate-review-state check, unreasonable-rate-increase threshold screen, exemption basis, log entry

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Compliance Officer; reviewed annually and on any CMS rate review bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — determination must close ahead of the annual QHP rate/plan submission window (opening in spring for a January 1 plan year) so the URRT can be built to the submission deadline

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts at each stage of the annual CMS rate/plan filing calendar — initial submission, correction window, final rate finalization around September — for every open determination

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Determination worksheet, threshold screen, effective-rate-review-state check and counsel sign-off retained 7 years from the rate's withdrawal from use

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any rate/form/rule implemented without a determination is logged as an exception with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every no-filing-required call and every late/unfiled remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every individual-market ACA rate, form and rule change with an effective date inside the test period, by issuer and state, per the policy admin change log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any implemented change with no determination on file before its effective date is a fail; any fail escalates to the Compliance Officer

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-filing; test runs quarterly over that quarter's population plus 100% of rows flagged at/above the unreasonable-rate-increase threshold

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing-determination test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Determination log export plus SERFF tracking numbers and disposition, presentable as a market conduct or rate review exam response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Counsel owns the exam/inquiry response and clears any admission of an unfiled change before it is sent

checklist.step: Take in the proposed change and open a determination worksheet
actions: Open the product change queue and filter for individual-market ACA changes awaiting a filing-requirement determination.
Record product name, issuer/NAIC co-code, market (individual on- or off-exchange), affected states, target plan year and proposed effective date, typically January 1.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager for the business driver — annual rate cycle, benefit-design update, mid-year correction — and record it.
Attach the change request to a determination folder named <issuer>-<state>-<plan year>.
checklist.done: the worksheet carries product, issuer, states, plan year and effective date, with the change request attached.

checklist.step: Classify the change as rate, form or rule
actions: Tag each element RATE (premium rates, rating factors, service-area rate table), FORM (Evidence of Coverage, Summary of Benefits and Coverage, riders, notices) or RULE (cost-sharing structure, benefit design, eligibility rule).
For RATE elements, confirm whether the change is an annual rate-cycle filing or an off-cycle rate change.
For RULE elements affecting cost-sharing reduction plan variants, flag for CSR-specific review since CSR variations carry their own benefit-design rules.
Record the tag and CSR flag on the worksheet row.
checklist.done: every change element is tagged and CSR-affecting rule changes are flagged.

checklist.step: Confirm Unified Rate Review Template applicability
actions: Determine whether the rate change triggers URRT Parts I-III submission, which applies to every single-risk-pool rate change in the individual market regardless of the percentage increase.
Confirm the market-wide index rate build reflects the single risk pool per 45 CFR 156.80.
Record the URRT applicability conclusion and its basis on the worksheet.
checklist.done: URRT applicability is determined and documented for the rate element.

checklist.step: Screen against the unreasonable-rate-increase threshold
actions: Compute the proposed rate increase percentage weighted-average across the affected plans.
Compare to the CMS unreasonable-rate-increase review threshold under 45 CFR 154.200/154.230.
Where the increase meets or exceeds the threshold, flag the filing for enhanced actuarial memorandum content and potential CMS/state review.
Record the computed percentage and threshold comparison on the worksheet.
checklist.done: the threshold screen is computed and documented, with any at/above-threshold filing flagged.

checklist.step: Check whether the state has an effective rate review program
actions: Consult the current CMS list of states with an effective rate review program versus states where CMS performs the review directly.
Record which entity, state DOI or CMS, performs the substantive rate review for each affected state.
Note any state-specific prior-approval or file-and-use requirement layered on top of the federal rate review.
checklist.done: the reviewing authority and the state's own filing type are recorded for every affected state.

checklist.step: Read each state's current SERFF filing rules for the ACA individual-market TOI
actions: Log in to SERFF and from the Industry menu open Filing Rules for the state, selecting the Health TOI/Sub-TOI matching individual ACA-compliant products.
Read the General Instructions and any state-specific Rate/Form filing checklist referenced.
Print the instructions to PDF, name it <state>-filing-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it as the evidence behind the review-method call.
Repeat for every affected state.
checklist.done: a dated filing-rules capture exists for every affected state.

checklist.step: Determine the filing requirement per element per state
actions: On each worksheet row, record the required filing type: rate filing (URRT + actuarial memo), form filing, or combined rate-and-form filing.
Cite the exact CFR section and/or state statute relied on.
Where a rule change requires no separate state filing but does require a CMS QHP application update, note the QHP-application-only path.
checklist.done: every element/state row states the required filing type with a citation.

checklist.step: Search SERFF Filing Access for an existing approval covering the change
actions: In SERFF Filing Access, search by NAIC co-code, state, TOI and form number for the most recent approved filing.
Compare the approved rate table/form edition to the proposed change.
Decide reuse (no new filing needed) versus new filing required, and record the SERFF Tracking Number if reusing.
checklist.done: each row states reuse (with tracking number) or new filing required, based on an inspected prior filing.

checklist.step: Support any no-filing-required call with a named exemption or CMS-only path
actions: Name the basis, such as an internal administrative correction with no rate/benefit impact or a CMS QHP application field update only.
Cite the CFR section or CMS guidance supporting the exemption.
Never leave a row reading only 'not required.'
checklist.done: every exempt row carries a named basis and citation.

checklist.step: Write the determination into the ACA Filing Determination Log
actions: For every state/element, log: change ID, state, element, filing required Y/N, filing type, URRT applicability, threshold screen result, reviewing authority, statutory cite, and decision date.
Link the log row to the determination folder.
Set status to Determined-pending-counsel or Determined-closed.
checklist.done: the log holds a complete, source-linked row per state per element.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel sign-off on threshold-flagged and no-filing-required rows
actions: Re-read the cited CFR sections and confirm or overturn each flagged determination in writing.
Send overturned rows back to the Product Filing Specialist for rework.
Date-stamp confirmed rows closed.
checklist.done: no threshold-flagged or exempt row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Notify Product Operations and Actuarial of the confirmed filing requirement
actions: Publish the determination summary to the product change record.
Flag every state requiring URRT submission and enhanced actuarial memorandum content for the Product / Filing Actuary.
Hand the confirmed state/filing-type list to the Insurance Product Manager to seed the release gate.
checklist.done: the determination is published and the Insurance Product Manager has the confirmed state/filing-type list.

checklist.step: Escalate when CMS threshold review timing conflicts with the plan-year deadline
actions: Compare the enhanced-review timeline for at/above-threshold filings to the annual CMS rate/plan finalization deadline.
Where the timeline is at risk, escalate to the Chief Risk Officer and product sponsor.
Record the decision — revise the rate ask, extend timeline, or accept delayed availability — on the log row.
checklist.done: every at-risk threshold filing has a written, owned decision.

checklist.step: Retain the determination evidence
actions: Move the determination folder — worksheet, filing-rules captures, threshold screen, counsel sign-off — into the compliance evidence repository under issuer and plan year.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Confirm the repository index shows the record searchable by state and SERFF tracking number.
checklist.done: the determination record is filed, labelled and retrievable by state and tracking number.

checklist.step: Log any implemented-without-determination change as an exception
actions: Compare the policy admin/rating change log against the determination log monthly.
Log any implemented change with no matching determination as an exception with root cause.
Route to Regulatory Counsel for a late-filing or self-report assessment.
checklist.done: every implemented-without-determination change is logged with root cause and a counsel assessment.

testing.step: Build the population of changes implemented in the period
actions: Extract every individual-market ACA rate, form and rule change with an effective date inside the test period, by issuer and state.
Include QHP application field updates alongside SERFF filings.
Reconcile to the CMS rate/plan finalization release notes for the plan year.
testing.done: population reconciled to CMS release records.

testing.step: Reconcile every implemented change to a pre-dated determination
actions: Match each population row to a determination log row on change ID + state + element.
Check the determination decision date pre-dates the change's effective date.
List unmatched or late determinations as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every population row matches a pre-dated determination or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of rows flagged at/above the unreasonable-rate-increase threshold.
Take a random sample of 20 additional rows (seeded, reproducible), minimum 30 rows total.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible, covering all threshold-flagged rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the URRT applicability and threshold screen
actions: Independently recompute the weighted-average rate increase for each sampled rate row from the underlying rate exhibits.
Compare to the recorded threshold screen result; any difference is an exception.
Confirm the URRT applicability conclusion is correct.
testing.done: independent threshold recomputation matches the recorded result or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the filing-requirement determination in SERFF
actions: Open SERFF Filing Rules for the sampled state and TOI as of the determination date.
Reach an independent filing-type conclusion without viewing the worksheet first.
Compare to the recorded determination; log any difference including 'right answer, wrong citation.'
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent re-performance note and a captured source page.

testing.step: Test the support behind no-filing-required calls
actions: Pull each exempt row and read the cited CFR section or CMS guidance as it read on the determination date.
Confirm the exemption genuinely covers the element filed under it.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off pre-dates the go-live date.
testing.done: every exempt row is supported by a verified citation and dated counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Trace every filing-required row to a real SERFF submission
actions: Search the recorded SERFF Tracking Number in Filing Access for the sampled row.
Confirm the filing exists for the right issuer, state, TOI and rate/form edition.
Compare the disposition date to the change's effective date.
testing.done: every filing-required row traces to a real SERFF filing submitted before go-live.

testing.step: Recompute the URRT figures independently
actions: For 10 sampled rate rows, independently rebuild the URRT Part I index rate and rate change figures from the source rate exhibits.
Compare to the figures actually submitted to CMS.
Log any material variance.
testing.done: independently rebuilt URRT figures match the submitted filing or a variance is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception.
Assign root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items to the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance-for-unfiled-change threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled determination, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Open the package build from the closed determination
actions: Pull the closed determination log rows for the filing and confirm filing type (rate/form/combined) and affected states.
Create a package folder per state named <issuer>-<state>-<plan year>-package.
Copy the companion-item checklist template into each folder.
checklist.done: a package folder with the companion-item checklist exists for every state in the closed determination.

checklist.step: Build the URRT Part I Rate Increase Summary
actions: In the actuarial platform, populate URRT Part I with the market-wide index rate, plan-adjusted index rates and the rate change per plan.
Validate the file against the CMS URRT XML schema validator before export.
Export the Part I workbook and attach to the package folder.
checklist.done: URRT Part I is built, schema-validated and attached to the package.

checklist.step: Build the URRT Part II rate table template and Part III actuarial memorandum
actions: Populate the rate table template with every rating factor — age, tobacco, geography — required by the state's rating rules.
Draft the actuarial memorandum narrative covering trend, benefit changes, risk adjustment/reinsurance impact and administrative expense load.
Cross-check every dollar figure in the memorandum against the URRT Part I/II exports.
checklist.done: Parts II and III are drafted and reconcile line-by-line to the URRT exports.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial certification
actions: Draft the certification statement confirming the filing complies with ASOPs and CMS URRT instructions and that the rates are not unreasonable, excessive, inadequate or unfairly discriminatory.
Have the Appointed Actuary review the certification for consistency with the annual statement's actuarial opinion.
Sign and date the certification.
checklist.done: a signed, dated actuarial certification is attached to the package.

checklist.step: Assemble the Plans & Benefits and Business Rules templates
actions: Complete the CMS Plans & Benefits template with the CSR variant structure, metal tier and EHB benchmark cross-walk for every plan.
Complete the Business Rules template with enrollment periods, service area and eligibility rules.
Confirm every CSR plan variation is represented and matches the actuarial memorandum's CSR load.
checklist.done: Plans & Benefits and Business Rules templates are complete and CSR variants reconcile to the actuarial memorandum.

checklist.step: Assemble state-specific companion items
actions: From the state's filing-rules checklist, gather the cover letter, transmittal form, Statement of Variability, readability/Flesch certification, and any state rate-summary worksheet.
Confirm the filing fee amount and payment method for the state and route to Accounts Payable Specialist.
Name the owner and due date for any outstanding companion item.
checklist.done: every state's companion-item list is fully assembled or has a named owner and due date for the remainder.

checklist.step: Assemble the redline package
actions: Produce a side-by-side redline of every changed form against its currently approved edition.
Confirm form numbers and edition dates are updated on every changed page.
Attach the redline set to the package.
checklist.done: a complete redline set is attached showing every form change against the approved edition.

checklist.step: Run the package QC checklist
actions: Verify every required companion item from the state checklist is present in the package folder.
Confirm all PDFs are text-searchable, watermark-free and under the SERFF attachment size cap.
Confirm the URRT export, actuarial memorandum and rate tables reconcile to each other.
Sign the QC checklist.
checklist.done: the QC checklist is complete and signed with no missing companion items.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Actuary review of the actuarial content
actions: Review the URRT, actuarial memorandum and certification for internal consistency and reasonableness.
Confirm the trend and benefit-change assumptions align with the company's pricing methodology on file.
Approve or return the actuarial content for rework.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has approved the actuarial content in writing.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel review of the legal/compliance content
actions: Review the cover letter, transmittal and Statement of Variability for accuracy against the underlying forms.
Confirm no representation in the package conflicts with a prior state finding or open CAP item.
Approve or return for rework.
checklist.done: Regulatory Counsel has approved the package's legal/compliance content.

checklist.step: Stage the package in SERFF
actions: Create the SERFF filing shell for the state, TOI/Sub-TOI, and attach every approved package component to the correct SERFF attachment slot.
Populate the SERFF General Information tab (filing type, effective date, filing fee) to match the package.
Save as draft and route to Product Filing Specialist for final release approval.
checklist.done: the SERFF filing shell is fully populated with every package component attached and saved as draft.

checklist.step: Get final release approval before submission
actions: Confirm the QC checklist, Chief Actuary approval and Regulatory Counsel approval are all on file.
Confirm the target submission date still allows the state's full review/deemer period before the target effective date.
Approve release of the draft SERFF filing for submission.
checklist.done: release is approved only after QC, actuarial and legal sign-off are all confirmed.

checklist.step: Version-control the package
actions: Lock the approved package version in the package folder and label it submission-ready.
Log any post-lock change as a new version with a change reason.
Confirm the version submitted in SERFF matches the locked submission-ready version.
checklist.done: the submitted SERFF package matches the locked, labelled submission-ready version.

checklist.step: Log any missing companion item found at submission as an exception
actions: If SERFF or the state rejects the filing for a missing item, log the rejection with root cause.
Assign an owner and target date to cure the deficiency and resubmit.
Update the QC checklist template if the gap reveals a systemic checklist error.
checklist.done: any submission rejection for a missing item is logged with root cause, owner and a checklist-template fix where applicable.

checklist.step: Retain the final package and approvals
actions: File the locked package, QC checklist, Chief Actuary approval, Regulatory Counsel approval and actuarial certification in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by issuer, state and plan year.
checklist.done: the final package and all approvals are filed, retention-labeled and searchable.

testing.step: Build the population of packages submitted in the period
actions: Extract every SERFF filing submitted in the test period for individual-market ACA rate/form filings.
Reconcile the count to the closed-determination log for the same period.
Include any non-SERFF state-portal submissions in the population extract.
testing.done: population reconciles to the closed-determination log.

testing.step: Reconcile each submitted package to its QC checklist
actions: Match each submitted filing to its package folder's signed QC checklist.
List any filing with no signed QC checklist as an exception.
Confirm the QC checklist's sign-off date pre-dates the SERFF submission date-stamp.
testing.done: every submitted filing has a matching signed QC checklist or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of packages that were rejected or required resubmission.
Take a random sample of 15 additional packages (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible, covering all rejected/resubmitted packages.

testing.step: Re-perform the URRT/memorandum reconciliation
actions: Independently trace the actuarial memorandum's key figures — index rate, rate change percentage, trend — to the submitted URRT export for each sampled package.
Log any figure that does not reconcile.
Confirm the rate table template's factor values match the figures cited in the memorandum narrative.
testing.done: URRT and memorandum figures reconcile on the sample or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Verify actuarial certification and Chief Actuary approval
actions: Confirm a signed, dated actuarial certification exists for each sampled package.
Confirm the Chief Actuary's written approval pre-dates the SERFF submission date.
Confirm the certifying actuary is credentialed (FSA/MAAA or equivalent) and named correctly on the certification.
testing.done: certification and approval exist and pre-date submission, or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Verify companion-item completeness against the state checklist
actions: Pull the current state filing-rules checklist for each sampled state.
Compare to the actual SERFF attachments and confirm every required item is present.
Confirm the filing fee amount and payment method on file match what the checklist requires for that state.
testing.done: companion items are complete against the state checklist or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Confirm Regulatory Counsel review
actions: Confirm a dated counsel approval exists for each sampled package pre-dating submission.
Spot-check the cover letter and Statement of Variability against the actual forms for accuracy.
Confirm no sampled package conflicts with an open CAP item or a prior state finding.
testing.done: counsel review is confirmed on the sample or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the CSR variant cross-walk
actions: For sampled CSR-bearing plans, independently confirm the Plans & Benefits template's CSR variant AV matches the actuarial memorandum's CSR load assumption.
Log any mismatch.
Confirm the CMS-assigned variant plan IDs referenced in the package match the Plans & Benefits template.
testing.done: CSR variant cross-walk is confirmed or a mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception.
Assign root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items to the next test cycle.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception/rejection rate and compare to the zero-rejection target.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who reviewed no sampled package, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the package is release-approved and submission-ready
actions: Pull the submission-ready locked package version and confirm the final release approval is on file.
Confirm the target submission date on the filing calendar still leaves the state's full review/deemer period before September 30 finalization.
Log the intended submission date on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: a release-approved, submission-ready package with a logged intended submission date exists.

checklist.step: Submit the filing in SERFF
actions: Open the staged SERFF filing shell, verify the attachment list against the QC checklist one final time, and click Submit.
Record the SERFF Tracking Number and submission date/time stamp.
Confirm the SERFF confirmation email is received and filed.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted with a recorded tracking number and confirmation on file.

checklist.step: Submit via any non-SERFF state portal where applicable
actions: For states taking the line outside SERFF, log in to the state's own filing portal and complete the state-specific submission form.
Upload the same package components in the state's required format.
Record the state's own tracking/confirmation number.
checklist.done: non-SERFF submissions carry a recorded state confirmation number.

checklist.step: Log the submission on the disposition tracker
actions: Add a row to the filing disposition tracker: state, tracking number, submission date, filing type, target effective date and expected disposition date (submission date plus review period).
Link the tracker row to the package folder.
Set the tracker row's initial status to Submitted.
checklist.done: every submission has a disposition tracker row with an expected disposition date.

checklist.step: Monitor SERFF/state portal status daily
actions: Check SERFF Filing Access status — Submitted, Pending, Deficient, Filed, Approved, Rejected — for every open filing each business day.
Check the equivalent status field on any non-SERFF state portal.
Update the disposition tracker status field to match.
checklist.done: the disposition tracker status is current as of each business day's check.

checklist.step: Respond to objections/deficiency letters within the state's SLA
actions: Read the objection letter in SERFF and route substantive actuarial/legal points to the Product / Filing Actuary or Regulatory Counsel.
Draft the response and any corrected exhibits within the state's stated response window, commonly 10 business days.
Submit the response through SERFF and log the response date and content summary on the tracker.
checklist.done: every objection has a documented, on-time response logged on the tracker.

checklist.step: Escalate any objection response at risk of missing its SLA
actions: Compare each open objection's due date to today plus the drafting time needed.
Escalate to the Chief Risk Officer any objection at risk within 2 business days of its due date.
Record the escalation and resulting action on the tracker row.
checklist.done: every at-risk objection response has a logged escalation and resulting action.

checklist.step: Record final disposition on approval, filed status, or deemer
actions: On SERFF status changing to Filed/Approved/Closed, capture the disposition date and, for prior-approval states, the approval letter.
Where a state's review period lapses with no objection (deemer), compute and record the deemer-satisfied date per the state's statutory review period.
Update the tracker status to Disposed with the disposition type and date.
checklist.done: every filing shows a recorded disposition type and date, including deemer computations where applicable.

checklist.step: Handle a rejection or withdrawal
actions: On a Rejected status, read the state's rejection basis and determine whether to cure and resubmit or withdraw.
Route the cure decision through the Product / Filing Actuary and Regulatory Counsel.
Log the rejection, cure/withdrawal decision and any resubmission tracking number on the tracker.
checklist.done: every rejection has a logged basis, decision and, if cured, a resubmission tracking number.

checklist.step: Reconcile disposed filings against the CMS annual rate/plan finalization deadline
actions: Compare each state's disposition date to the CMS annual finalization deadline of September 30.
Flag any state not yet disposed as September 30 approaches.
Escalate undisposed states to the Compliance Officer immediately once flagged.
checklist.done: every state's disposition status is reconciled against the September 30 deadline with flags escalated.

checklist.step: Finalize QHP rate and plan data with CMS by September 30
actions: For every disposed (approved or deemer-satisfied) state, confirm the corresponding QHP plan and rate data is finalized in the CMS system ahead of the September 30 finalization window.
Confirm no plan is finalized with rate/plan data that does not match its disposed SERFF filing.
Record the CMS finalization confirmation on the tracker.
checklist.done: CMS finalization is confirmed by September 30 and matches the disposed filing for every state.

checklist.step: Notify downstream teams of the disposed states and effective dates
actions: Publish the disposition summary — state, disposition type, date, effective date — to the Insurance Product Manager and Implementation Specialist.
Flag any state where a hold on release remains in force pending disposition.
Post the summary to the shared filing calendar so Product Operations can plan the go-live sequence.
checklist.done: downstream teams have the disposition summary and any active release holds are flagged.

checklist.step: Log any filing missing disposition past September 30 as an exception
actions: Log an exception for any filing still undisposed after the September 30 finalization cutoff.
Record root cause — state backlog, unresolved objection, missed response — and the current status.
Set a remediation date and escalate to the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: every undisposed filing past September 30 is logged with root cause, status and a remediation date.

checklist.step: Retain the disposition record
actions: File the submission confirmation, all objection correspondence, and the final disposition/approval letter or deemer computation in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Confirm the record is indexed by state and tracking number.
checklist.done: the disposition record is filed, retention-labeled and indexed.

checklist.step: Close out the filing tracker for the plan year
actions: Confirm every state row shows a final disposition status.
Archive the plan year's tracker and open a fresh tracker for the next plan year's filing cycle.
Report the closed cycle's on-time disposition rate to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: the plan year's tracker is fully disposed, archived and reported to the Compliance Committee.

testing.step: Build the population of filings submitted in the plan-year cycle
actions: Extract every SERFF and state-portal submission from the disposition tracker for the plan-year cycle.
Reconcile the count to the closed filing-package population from the preparation stage.
Confirm every affected state on the determination log has a corresponding submission record.
testing.done: population reconciles to the closed package population.

testing.step: Reconcile disposition status to SERFF/state portal directly
actions: Independently pull each filing's current status directly from SERFF Filing Access or the state portal.
Compare to the tracker's recorded status.
List any mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: SERFF/portal status matches the tracker or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of filings rejected, withdrawn, or still undisposed past September 30.
Take a random sample of 20 additional disposed filings (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible, covering all rejected/undisposed filings.

testing.step: Re-verify objection-response timeliness
actions: For sampled filings with an objection, compare the response submission date in SERFF to the state's stated SLA from the objection letter date.
Log any response that missed the SLA.
Confirm any escalation raised for an at-risk objection was recorded on the tracker with a resulting action.
testing.done: objection responses are within SLA on the sample or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Recompute deemer-satisfied dates
actions: For sampled deemer-based dispositions, recompute the deemer-satisfied date from the state's statutory review period and the submission date.
Compare to the recorded date and to the effective date used in CMS finalization.
Confirm the statutory review-period length used matches the current state instructions, not a stale figure.
testing.done: recomputed deemer dates match the recorded figures or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Trace disposed states to CMS finalization
actions: Confirm the CMS-finalized QHP plan/rate data for each sampled disposed state matches the disposed SERFF filing's rate table and plan design.
Confirm the finalization date is on or before September 30.
Flag any finalized state whose CMS data pre-dates its SERFF disposition, which would indicate finalization jumped the gun.
testing.done: CMS finalization matches the disposed filing and pre-dates September 30, or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Test rejection/withdrawal handling
actions: Review each sampled rejection's basis, cure/withdrawal decision and any resubmission.
Confirm the decision was documented and the resubmission, if any, reflects the cure.
Confirm a withdrawal decision was communicated to the product sponsor and reflected in the release plan.
testing.done: rejection handling is properly documented and cured, or a finding is logged.

testing.step: Verify release holds were respected until disposition
actions: For sampled states, confirm the policy admin/rating system shows no use of the new rate/form before the recorded disposition or deemer-satisfied date.
Log any use before disposition as a compliance breach, not a routine exception.
Where a breach is found, trace the affected policy count and route it to Compliance Officer for a self-report assessment.
testing.done: no sampled state was used before disposition, or a breach is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception.
Assign root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into the next cycle's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time disposition rate against the September 30 finalization target.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who tracked no sampled filing, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion exists in the repository.
